title: Nanosecond-Precision Pick Submission Lock Time Validation
i_want: Clear and fair handling when submitting picks at the exact lock time with nanosecond precision
so_that: I understand whether my pick was accepted or rejected based on precise timing rules, with grace periods for network latency

acceptance_criteria.scenario: Pick submitted exactly at lock time with grace period
given: System configured with 2-second grace period for network latency
User submits pick at 13:00:01.500000000 UTC (1.5s after lock)
when: Server receives request with client timestamp
Server timestamp is 13:00:01.600000000 UTC (100ms server delay)
System compares both timestamps against lock time + grace period
then: Pick is accepted because within 2-second grace period
Response includes: 'Pick accepted (grace period applied due to network delay)'
Database stores: submission_timestamp, server_timestamp, lock_timestamp, grace_applied=true
Audit log records: latency=600ms, grace_remaining=400ms
User sees success message with timestamp details

acceptance_criteria.scenario: Pick submitted after grace period expires
given: Grace period is 2 seconds (ends at 13:00:02.000000000 UTC)
when: Server validates timestamp against lock + grace period
Submission is 100ms after grace period expiration
then: Pick is rejected with HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity
Error code: 'PICK_SUBMITTED_AFTER_LOCK'
Message: 'Pick rejected: Game locked at 1:00 PM. Your submission arrived 2.1 seconds after lock time (grace period: 2.0s).'
Response includes: lock_time, submission_time, grace_period, time_difference
UI shows clear countdown timer next time to prevent repeat
No partial data is stored in database

acceptance_criteria.scenario: Concurrent picks for same game by same user
given: User submits pick for Cowboys at 12:59:58 UTC
Due to network issue, client retries at 12:59:59 UTC
Both requests arrive at server within 200ms
when: Second request (Cowboys retry) arrives before first commits
System detects duplicate submission via idempotency key
then: First request completes successfully
Second request returns HTTP 200 with cached response from first request
Message: 'Pick already submitted successfully for this game'
Database contains exactly one pick record
Both requests have same idempotency_key in logs
No 'duplicate pick' error shown to user

acceptance_criteria.scenario: Clock skew between client and server
given: Client clock is 5 seconds ahead of server (misconfigured device)
User submits at 12:59:57 UTC (server time) but client shows 13:00:02
when: Server uses server timestamp as authoritative
Client timestamp included for logging only
then: Pick is accepted based on server timestamp (within grace period)
Warning logged: 'Client clock skew detected: +5.0 seconds'
Response includes: server_time, client_time, skew_detected=true
Metrics track clock skew distribution for monitoring
UI potentially warns user about clock synchronization

acceptance_criteria.scenario: High-load scenario with 1000 picks in final second
given: 1000 users submit picks between 12:59:59.000 and 13:00:00.999 UTC
Server must process all requests fairly
when: Picks arrive with timestamps distributed across final second
Queue processes requests in timestamp order (not arrival order)
Some requests delayed by up to 500ms due to load
then: All picks with (server_timestamp - latency) < lock_time + grace_period are accepted
Picks are processed in submission timestamp order
Queue processing time < 100ms per pick at p99
Total processing time for 1000 picks < 5 minutes
No picks lost or corrupted
Real-time progress updates sent to users via WebSocket
Metrics show: queue_depth, processing_rate, latency_distribution

acceptance_criteria.scenario: Grace period configuration by league commissioner
given: League commissioner can configure grace period (0-30 seconds)
Default is 2 seconds for standard leagues
High-stakes leagues may use 0 seconds (strict enforcement)
when: Commissioner sets grace period to 5 seconds
Setting takes effect for all future game locks
Existing scheduled locks updated with new grace period
then: All pick validations use 5-second grace period
UI shows grace period on game lock countdown
Email notifications mention grace period policy
Audit log records grace period changes with timestamp
Users notified of grace period policy changes

timestamp_precision.storage: TIMESTAMP(9) or BIGINT nanoseconds since epoch

idempotency.storage: Redis with TTL = lock_time + grace_period + 5 minutes
idempotency.duplicate_detection: Check idempotency key before database write
idempotency.concurrent_handling: Return cached response for duplicate requests

clock_skew_handling.authoritative_source: Server timestamp always used for validation
clock_skew_handling.ntp_recommendation: Suggest NTP sync to clients with large skew

queue_processing.priority_queue: Sort by submission timestamp (not arrival time)
queue_processing.retry: 3 attempts with exponential backoff for transient failures
queue_processing.dead_letter_queue: Failed picks after retries for manual review

late_submission.message: Pick rejected: Game locked at {lock_time}. Your submission arrived {delay} after lock time (grace period: {grace_period}).
late_submission.user_action: No retry allowed for this game

grace_period_accepted.message: Pick accepted (grace period applied due to network delay)

clock_skew_warning.warning: Your device clock is {skew} seconds ahead/behind server time. This may affect submission timing.
clock_skew_warning.recommendation: Please synchronize your device clock with NTP.

performance_requirements.throughput: Handle 10,000 picks per minute during peak times

alerts: Clock skew > 10 seconds for > 1% of users
dashboards: Real-time pick submission timeline (last 60 seconds before lock)
Grace period application rate by game
Clock skew heatmap by user geography

load_testing: Simulate 10,000 users submitting picks in final 10 seconds before lock
Test grace period edge cases: exactly at boundary, 1ns before/after
Verify queue ordering with shuffled arrival times
Measure latency distribution under peak load
time_testing: Mock clock to test nanosecond-precision comparisons
Test all clock skew scenarios: +/- 1s, +/- 10s, +/- 1 hour
edge_cases: Pick submitted at exactly lock_time + grace_period (boundary)
Concurrent picks with same idempotency key
Database failure during pick processing (rollback verification)
integration_tests: End-to-end pick submission with real timestamps
Redis idempotency key expiration and cleanup

countdown_timer.grace_period_indicator: Show grace period in yellow zone on timer
warnings: Yellow alert at 30 seconds before lock
Red alert at 10 seconds before lock
Disable submit button at lock + grace period

Queue system (e.g., BullMQ, RabbitMQ) for high-load processing
